cases.question: Compare the top three open-source vector databases for a startup building RAG products.
cases.expected: Compares three open-source vector databases; vendor claims stay attributed and unsupported superlatives are dropped.
agent_plan_criteria: Eligibility: Must be an open‑source project (permissive or copyleft license) that provides a vector search engine suitable for embeddings.
Popularity / adoption: Relative community size, star count, number of forks, and presence in recent RAG tutorials or reference architectures.
Performance: Reported query latency, throughput, and scalability for typical embedding dimensions (e.g., 768‑1536).
Community & ecosystem: Frequency of releases, active issue/PR turnover, availability of connectors (Python, LangChain, LlamaIndex) and documentation quality.
Licensing suitability for a commercial startup: Whether the license permits proprietary use without viral obligations and any required attribution.

claims.text: Milvus, pgvector and Weaviate are described as open-source vector-search projects, but the sources do not establish a current relative adoption ranking.
claims.issue: The cited evidence does not state this.
quotes: Open-source vector databases include Milvus, Weaviate, Qdrant, PGVector, Chroma, and FAISS.
pgvector is an open-source extension that adds vector search to PostgreSQL. If you already run Postgres, you can add vector capabilities without a new database.
Weaviate: An open-source graph-based vector store.

claims.text: Milvus says it reached more than 35,000 GitHub stars. Without comparable, current metrics for the other projects, that claim does not establish its relative rank.
claims.issue: The cited evidence does not state this.
quotes: Our Journey to 35K+ GitHub Stars: The Real Story of Building Milvus from Scratch

claims.text: An aggregator reports that Milvus has Python SDKs and LangChain and LlamaIndex integrations. ZenML says its pipelines can connect to Milvus, pgvector and Weaviate.
quotes: The project provides client SDKs for Python, Java, Go, and other languages, as well as integration with popular AI models and ML frameworks, including LangChain and LlamaIndex.

With ZenML, you can plug in any vector database you prefer, whether Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, Milvus, or even Postgres with pgvector, and focus on building reliable, fine-tuned production-ready pipelines.

claims.text: A reported benchmark combines pgvector with pgvectorscale; it does not provide a like-for-like comparison of the three options. Vendor benchmark conditions can vary.
claims.issue: Parts of the claim go beyond the cited evidence.
quotes: Per Tiger Data's benchmarks (formerly Timescale), pgvector with pgvectorscale achieved 28x lower p95 latency and 16x higher query throughput compared to Pinecone's storage-optimized (s1) index at 99% recall on 50M 768-dim embeddings (self-hosted).
Vendor benchmarks are marketing tools. Conditions vary (hardware, dataset size, recall targets), and every vendor optimizes for scenarios that favor their product.

claims.text: Benchmark shortlisted options against the startup's own workload, including writes, metadata filters and concurrency, before choosing.
claims.issue: The cited evidence does not state this.
quotes: Vendor benchmarks are marketing tools. Conditions vary (hardware, dataset size, recall targets), and every vendor optimizes for scenarios that favor their product.
Leaderboards reward performance under static conditions, yet production systems must survive continuous writes, metadata filters, and concurrency spikes.
